claims.statement: Skin graft survival requires vascular support and close contact with the recipient surface.
claims.limitation: No universal technical protocol, exact probability, dose or healing-time guarantee is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A nonviable bare tendon or bone surface cannot support direct skin grafting merely because neighboring tissue is vascular.
claims.limitation: One adequate review; the constructed record must identify the actual uncovered surface, not merely name a prior injury.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Graft suitability is reassessed from the current vascularized recipient surface; a historical avascular surface does not describe a later prepared bed.
claims.limitation: Original clinical application of bed-dependence; no claim that all bare cortex predictably develops a graftable covering. Mixed beds remain non-equivalent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A fluid collection separating a new graft from its bed can obstruct take and requires timely correction.
claims.limitation: One adequate review; an original fluid pocket is supplied, not inferred from discoloration alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Motion between a new graft and its bed can disrupt early vascular connections; fixation protects apposition.
claims.limitation: No universal technical protocol, exact probability, dose or healing-time guarantee is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Greater retained dermal thickness reduces later graft contraction relative to a thinner graft, but increases recipient support requirements.
claims.limitation: No universal technical protocol, exact probability, dose or healing-time guarantee is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Partial-thickness donor wounds can re-epithelialize from retained cutaneous epithelial appendages.
claims.limitation: One current direct review, corroborated by locally verified donor/hair-follicle ledgers; no fixed healing time.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A full-thickness skin graft removes the dermal epithelial reservoirs with the skin, so its donor defect generally requires surgical closure.
claims.limitation: One adequate reconstructive review; no claim that every donor can be closed directly under arbitrary tension.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Purple swelling, brisk dark bleeding and rapid refill can indicate flap venous compromise even with persistent arterial inflow.
claims.limitation: Low-level heterogeneous clinical literature. Do not infer a specific thrombus from skin observations alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A threatened free flap with a potentially correctable mechanical outflow problem warrants urgent microsurgical exploration.
claims.limitation: One adequate systematic review, largely observational evidence. No fixed salvage deadline or specific revision technique claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Medicinal leeches may temporarily offload venous blood when surgical correction is unsuitable; they do not repair an obstructed pedicle or restore arterial inflow.
claims.limitation: FDA indication corroborates mechanism, not comparative superiority. Specialist judgment and monitored hospital care are prerequisites.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Localized bleeding can persist after a medicinal leech detaches and can produce clinically important blood loss.
claims.limitation: No blood-loss volume, monitoring interval or transfusion cutoff is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Residual devitalized or heavily contaminated tissue can favor initial open care and reassessment rather than immediate skin approximation.
claims.limitation: Single older review; no universal wound-age rule, cleansing pressure, exact closure day or infection treatment regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Later approximation after an initial open interval is delayed primary closure when reassessment supports viable clean edges.
claims.limitation: Single older review; ongoing open contraction without planned approximation is a different healing course.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Keloid scar overgrowth extends beyond the original wound; hypertrophic scar stays within its boundary.
claims.limitation: No universal technical protocol, exact probability, dose or healing-time guarantee is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A scar causing substantial fixed functional contracture can require reconstructive release rather than treatment of elevation alone.
claims.limitation: Consensus guidance; no universal delay to surgery or single required incision design. Functional examination must locate skin tethering.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Rapidly growing or otherwise atypical scar-like lesions warrant tissue diagnosis when a tumor is suspected before scar treatment.
claims.limitation: Consensus source; benign or malignant histology is not established by appearance alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Intralesional triamcinolone is an established treatment for symptomatic raised pathological scars.

claims.statement: Selected recurrent keloids considered for excision require a planned recurrence-reduction adjunct rather than excision as a self-contained cure.

claims.limitation: Current US guidance; do not generalize the HIV/severe-immunodeficiency exception to every immune-modifying drug.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: For dirty wounds after a complete primary series, a tetanus booster is indicated at five or more years since the last dose.
claims.limitation: Current US CDC prose and flowchart agree for dirty wounds; a constructed six-year interval is an example, not a new cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Restricted vitamin C intake can cause capillary-fragility signs and impaired wound healing, and plasma vitamin C is used to assess status.
claims.limitation: No diagnosis from slow healing alone and no exact supplementation regimen. Distinct from general energy/protein prescription, which belongs to nutrition.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Wound remodeling shifts an early type-III-rich collagen matrix toward greater type I representation; epithelial closure does not prove normal deeper mechanical strength.
claims.limitation: No return-to-work clearance, exact duration or tensile-strength percentage is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A CBC includes hemoglobin and can help assess or monitor anemia in a patient with suspected blood loss.
claims.limitation: A CBC alone does not identify the cause, prescribe a transfusion or set a monitoring interval.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed clinic or outside-record review cases.

claims.statement: Zinc contributes to wound healing; serum or plasma testing can assess status but needs clinical and nutritional context.
claims.limitation: Slow healing alone does not identify zinc deficiency. No zinc threshold or replacement dose is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed clinic or outside-record review cases.

claims.statement: Meshing can conserve limited donor skin for larger coverage but leaves interstices and can increase later contraction compared with smaller-mesh or sheet coverage.
claims.limitation: One review; no expansion ratio or universal best reconstruction is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed clinic or outside-record review cases.

claims.statement: Viable wound edges should not be forced into approximation under excessive tension; tissue availability affects whether closure or coverage is appropriate.
claims.limitation: No measured tension cutoff or procedure ranking beyond the specific constructed geometry.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed clinic or outside-record review cases.

claims.statement: A shellfish food reaction does not establish iodine as an allergen or by itself contraindicate a different iodine-containing product.
claims.limitation: One adequate surgical-allergy review for this cross-reactivity boundary. A true previous reaction to povidone-iodine itself would require its own assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a reported iodine allergy based on a shellfish food reaction.

claims.statement: Detachment alone does not establish graft necrosis; current tissue assessment informs retention after correction of an interface barrier.
claims.limitation: Original clinical application of the sources' vascularization and interface principles. Pink color and dermal bleeding are not a validated viability score or guarantee of salvage. The exact fictional examination and retained-tissue plan require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Finger tendon function should be assessed independently at the relevant joints; preserved composite movement does not exclude a partial flexor injury.
claims.limitation: Single government-sponsored expert commentary. Original maneuver wording describes separate PIP/DIP flexion against resistance; no protected illustration, exact injury percentage or operative threshold reproduced.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A limited negative hand ultrasound cannot exclude injury in a tendon segment the report explicitly did not visualize.
claims.limitation: Original application of the source's operator-dependent adjunctive imaging guidance to an explicitly unassessed segment; not a numerical sensitivity or diagnostic-accuracy claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A never-vaccinated person needs active tetanus immunization after a wound; TIG is separately determined by the wound category.
claims.limitation: Direct current CDC guidance. Formulation and subsequent valid-dose scheduling are outside this item; no recent-dose timing is left unstated.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: An acute tryptase above 1.2 times the recovered baseline plus 2 ng/mL supports event-associated mast-cell activation, without proving an IgE mechanism.
claims.limitation: Professional consensus criterion in perioperative guidance; clinical context remains essential. A result not exceeding it does not independently exclude anaphylaxis. No diagnosis of a particular culprit or mast-cell disorder follows.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

exactValueSupport.locator: Perioperative anaphylaxis section, PDF page40 (printed page39), paired tryptase interpretation

claims.statement: Guidance favors an acute tryptase sample early in a suspected event, ideally within two hours, with a later recovered baseline for comparison.
claims.limitation: Conditional timing guidance; the fictional 80-minute sample and well follow-up are observations, not new mandatory collection rules. No fixed result-wait duration is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: A previous negative latex-protein assay and a contact-allergy result do not determine the mechanism or culprit of a newly documented systemic event.
claims.limitation: Original clinical inference from distinct immediate/contact mechanisms and history-based event evaluation. No false-negative rate, mandatory retest interval or sensitization timeline is claimed; chronology prioritizes assessment without proving a culprit.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

claims.statement: Biopsy size and depth must address the suspected lesion; repeat sampling can be considered when the initial specimen is inadequate for diagnosis.
claims.limitation: Professional biopsy guidance plus scar-mimic consensus. No specific malignancy is diagnosed and no one biopsy technique is declared universally best. New sections cannot create anatomical tissue never acquired; that application is explicit clinical reasoning.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in clinic reviewing their wound or outside reconstructive records.

disagreements.issue: CDC clinical prose uses a ten-year clean-minor completed-series booster interval; its linked October2026 flowchart appears to use a five-year branch for clean/minor wounds.
disagreements.disposition: Do not author a scored clean/minor completed-series interval question. The clean-minor incomplete-series item is unaffected. Melissa should verify the discrepant official artifact before any such key.
disagreements.verificationLimit: Apparent branch conflict confirmed in retrieved text; screenshot tool did not expose an inspectable image. Melissa should check the official PDF visually. No threshold from the disputed branch is keyed.

disagreements.issue: NHS discourages routine keloid excision because of recurrence; specialist consensus describes excision with planned adjuncts for selected lesions.
disagreements.disposition: Retain population/treatment-scope difference. No universal surgical best-treatment claim; exact selected cases require clinician review.
